transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to raise a concern before we go further. I conducted a confidential student-safety review and found a substantiated retaliation concern involving two students in this election. Because of this, our student-privacy protocol requires anonymous voting and prohibits releasing vote totals until the election is certified. I've kept the review in my counseling file since it contains protected student information, and I hadn't yet briefed you on this. The current draft plan's online ballot and publication of vote totals at the end of election day may conflict with these requirements.

transcript.text: Thank you, Ms. Ellis and Ms. Romero. My concern directly relates to what Ms. Ellis has raised about anonymity. I tested the draft online ballot this morning and found that the platform records each voter's identity for 90 days, and that feature cannot be disabled. This means the online ballot cannot support the anonymous voting that Ms. Ellis's student-safety protocol requires. I've already confirmed an approved workaround: sealed paper ballots counted by two adults, with zero electronic voter records. However, I have not yet updated the election plan to reflect this workaround since the test. I recommend we revise the plan to replace the online ballot with the sealed paper ballot process before Dr. Morgan gives final approval.
